title: Only 7% Pass This Oxford Entrance Exam
summary: Arguments, assumptions and precise deductions test whether your reasoning can survive every hidden trap.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge contains ten Oxford-inspired reasoning questions across verbal, quantitative, critical, formal, spatial and evidence-based thinking. It moves from accessible foundations to compact multi-step problems.

Choose the answer best supported by the information shown. No specialist university knowledge is required, and correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.

This is not an official Oxford University admissions test, application assessment or prediction of admission.

steps: Complete ten carefully selected questions in one focused challenge.
Choose one answer each time. Correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.
Reveal your result, skill breakdown and complete answer review after the final question.

about.disclaimer: Independent entertainment challenge. Not an official Oxford admissions test and not affiliated with any university.

oxford-s1q1.question: ARCHIVE is to RECORDS as ANTHOLOGY is to…

oxford-s1q6.question: A book costs £24 after a 20% reduction. What was its original price?

oxford-s2q2.question: Of 100 students, 70 attend tutoring and 50 use the library. A student may do both, just one or neither. How many do both?

oxford-s2q4.question: A school says extending library opening hours will let more students use it. Which assumption best supports that claim?

answers.a1: Every student enjoys using the library
answers.a3: Longer opening hours always improve grades
answers.a4: Some students who cannot visit now would use the extra hours

oxford-s3q3.question: Exactly one statement is true. A says ‘B is true.’ B says ‘A and C are false.’ C says ‘B is false.’ Who is true?

oxford-s3q7.question: A square has a mark in its top-left corner. Rotate the square 180° around its centre. Where is the mark now?

oxford-s4q3.question: Which question exposes missing information in ‘Most students prefer tutorials’?

answers.a2: How many students were asked and how were they selected?

oxford-s4q4.question: A candidate must submit an application form and a recommendation letter. Mei submitted only the form. What can you conclude?

answers.a1: Mei has met all submission requirements
answers.a3: Mei has not yet met all submission requirements

oxford-s5q6.question: A library extends its evening hours, and visits rise. Which comparison best distinguishes the effect of the new hours from a seasonal increase?

answers.a1: Compare visits with a similar library that kept the same opening hours during that period
answers.a2: Ask visitors if they like evenings
answers.a4: Compare this month's visits with last month's visits

oxford-s5q7.question: A rule admits applicants with Logic ≥ 80 and Writing ≥ 70. Ava scores 84/68; Bo scores 79/90; Cy scores 82/74. Who qualifies?
